task.description:
Execute Step 2b (Design Gate) for WF03-ISS0761-20260924. HARD GATE.

Read lib/letflow/design/iss-0761-swiftroute-persona-actor-provisioning.md independently.

ISSUE ACs from docs/issues/ISS-0739.yaml:
- Persona actors (Lena/Marco/Alice) can sign in to QA and complete their respective tasks
- UAT-RUNNER can resolve these actors to credentials
- .claude/agents/uat-runner.md documents the credential resolution

For each AC, check: is there a concrete design element addressing it?
- Are the API payloads fully specified?
- Is the idempotency approach concrete?
- Is the Part A dependency (ai-dala-infra) stated clearly?
- Is any implementation code present? (FAIL if yes)

Complete handoff (step-02b-design-gate.json): status COMPLETED, result.status PASS or FAIL.
acceptance_criteria: All ACs addressed with concrete design elements

ac1_actors_can_sign_in_and_complete_task.note: §1 scopes Part A (Keycloak accounts) as an explicit external dependency on ai-dala-infra — not deferred/TBD, but correctly bounded. §4 maps each actor to their required group memberships so that once Part A exists, they can sign in and execute their tasks. Part A's absence is a documented pre-condition, not a gap in the design.

ac2_uat_runner_can_resolve_actors_to_cre.note: §5 provides the exact text to insert into .claude/agents/uat-runner.md, including what to check (GET /identity/users?search= empty items = Part A not done; GET /identity/roles missing role-ops-manager = Part B not run) and what action to take (BLOCKED/CREDENTIALS_MISSING, not a workaround).

ac3_uat_runner_md_documents_credential_r.note: §5 specifies exact insertion location ('immediately after the last paragraph of the Environment target section, after the Bilimbaga realm note, before ## Forbidden') and provides the full verbatim text block to insert. No ambiguity on where or what.

persona_mapping_explicit.note: §4 table is complete: lena→TASK_WORKER only; marco→TASK_WORKER+role-ops-manager; alice→TASK_WORKER+role-ceo. Rationale for each stated. TASK_WORKER group seeded-not-created constraint is explicit.

part_a_dependency_stated.note: §1 names the external owner (ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-login.sh), marks it as not in scope, states execution order, and specifies the abort error message if Part A has not been done when Part B runs.

uat_runner_md_update_location_and_text_s.note: See ac3 above — both location and verbatim text are present.

no_implementation_code.note: Code blocks in the design are: JSON request/response payload shapes (§2), jq filter patterns as algorithm specification (§3), and read-only curl verification commands (§6). No complete .sh script body, no .ex/.exs function implementations. §6 verification curls are presented as 'what the script should emit' (acceptance verification), not as implementation.

open_questions_assessment.OQ-1: Pre-implementation verification step for ELIXIR-DEV (confirm exact Keycloak username format against ai-dala-infra). Not a design gap — the mechanism is fully specified; the check is a concrete pre-coding step with clear decision rule. PASS.
open_questions_assessment.OQ-2: ELIXIR-DEV judgment call on optional display_name/description fields. Suggested defaults provided. Not blocking. PASS.
open_questions_assessment.OQ-3: Non-blocking awareness note for REVIEWER. Script has a clean abort on mismatch. PASS.
open_questions_assessment.OQ-4: Non-blocking naming consistency note. Design recommends reusing QA_AUTH_TOKEN. PASS.

result.summary: Design is complete and ready for implementation. All four API calls have full body shapes and success/idempotent response codes. All three ISS-0739 ACs are addressed with concrete design elements. Part A external dependency is clearly bounded. uat-runner.md update specifies both exact location and verbatim text. No implementation code present.
